message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of the bones of the head (skull):

## Overview

The human skull consists of **22 bones** (or 29 if including the inner ear bones and hyoid bone). These bones are primarily connected by immovable fibrous joints called **sutures**. The skull is divided into two main parts:

1. **Neurocranium (Cranium)** - the braincase that protects the brain
2. **Viscerocranium (Facial Skeleton)** - the bones that form the face

---

## Cranium (Neurocranium) - 8 Bones

The cranium forms the protective housing for the brain and consists of:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal bone** (1) | Forms the forehead and roof of the orbits; contains frontal sinuses |
| **Parietal bones** (2) | Form the sides and roof of the cranial vault |
| **Temporal bones** (2) | Form the sides and base; house middle and inner ear structures |
| **Occipital bone** (1) | Forms the back and base; contains the **foramen magnum** for spinal cord passage |
| **Sphenoid bone** (1) | Butterfly-shaped bone at the base; contains sella turcica (pituitary gland housing) |
| **Ethmoid bone** (1) | Located between orbits; forms part of nasal cavity and contains cribriform plate |

---

## Facial Skeleton (Viscerocranium) - 14 Bones

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Mandible** (1) | Lower jaw; the **only movable bone** of the skull |
| **Maxillae** (2) | Upper jaw; form part of orbit and most of hard palate |
| **Zygomatic bones** (2) | Cheekbones; form part of lateral orbital walls |
| **Nasal bones** (2) | Form the bridge of the nose |
| **Lacrimal bones** (2) | Small bones in medial orbital walls; house lacrimal sac |
| **Palatine bones** (2) | Form posterior part of hard palate |
| **Inferior nasal conchae** (2) | Project into nasal cavity; aid in airflow regulation |
| **Vomer** (1) | Forms inferior portion of nasal septum |

---

## Key Features

- **Cranial Sutures**: Coronal (frontal-parietal), Sagittal (between parietals), Lambdoid (parietal-occipital), Squamous (parietal-temporal)
- **Cranial Fossae**: Anterior, middle, and posterior cranial fossae that house different parts of the brain
- **Foramina**: Openings for nerves and blood vessels (e.g., foramen magnum, optic canal, jugular foramen)
- **Temporomandibular Joint (TMJ)**: The only synovial (movable) joint in the skull

---

## Additional Associated Bones

- **Hyoid bone** - Located in the neck; supports tongue and larynx muscles (not part of skull proper)
- **Auditory ossicles** (malleus, incus, stapes) - Tiny bones in the middle ear for sound transmission

---

Sources:
1. https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/the-skull
2. https://www.osmosis.org/learn/Bones_of_the_cranium
3. https://teachmeanatomy.info/head/osteology/skull/
4. https://www.numberanalytics.com/blog/skull-bones-anatomy-histology-explored
5. https://www.acibademhealthpoint.com/the-back-of-head-bones-understanding-cranial-anatomy/
6. https://anatomynote.com/the-human-skull-an-anatomical-masterpiece/
7. https://anatomy.co.uk/skull
8. https://www.imaios.com/en/vet-anatomy/anatomical-structures/bones-of-the-cranium-11073768800
